desc:
Flutter package and plugin development turns code you keep rewriting into a tested, documented library. Ecom Swift LLC builds Dart packages and Kotlin and Swift plugins for your own apps, your team or, if you choose, pub.dev.

## What is a Flutter package?

A Flutter package is a reusable bundle of Dart code with its own version, tests and documentation. It can hold widgets, helpers, an API client, a theme or business rules. A plugin is a special kind of package that also contains platform code, written in Kotlin for Android and Swift for iOS, so Flutter can reach features the framework does not offer directly.

Your apps add a package through the pubspec file, either from pub.dev or from a private git repository. When the package changes, each app can choose when to take the update.

## Why shared code deserves its own package

When two apps need the same login screen or the same payment logic, the easy route is to copy the files. It works until a bug appears. Then someone fixes it in one app and forgets the other, and the copies drift apart.

A package gives that code a single home. Fixes are made once, versions record what changed and tests protect the behavior. For agencies and teams with several apps, this is the difference between a library and a pile of copied folders. It also makes onboarding easier, because new developers read one README rather than reverse-engineering three projects.

## How reusable packages affect your results

The benefit is speed and consistency. A new app can start with your design system, your network layer and your analytics wrapper already in place, so developers spend their time on what is unique. Users meet the same buttons, spacing and behavior across your products.

Quality improves too. Code that has a public interface, tests and an example app is easier to review and harder to break by accident. Publishing to pub.dev, where you choose to, also lets other developers use and report on your work, though the choice of public or private is yours.

## What a good Flutter package includes

- A focused purpose: one package should do one job well.
- A small, clear public API with sensible names and little exposed internal detail.
- Unit tests for logic and widget tests for visual components.
- A README covering installation and a few brief examples of use.
- Dartdoc comments on public classes and methods.
- An example app that shows the package working on a real screen.
- A changelog and version tags following semantic versioning.
- A correct pubspec with dependency ranges that do not block your apps.
- Checks on both iOS and Android, and notes on other platforms where relevant.
- For plugins, platform code with a documented method channel or modern interface.

## How we build your package

We begin with the problem. We look at the code you want to reuse, or the feature you want to create, and decide what belongs inside the package and what stays in the app. Then we design the public interface first, because that is the part other developers live with.

Next we write the code, the tests and the documentation, and build an example app that exercises the interface. If the work needs platform code, we write and test the Kotlin and Swift parts. For larger packages, we add a continuous integration pipeline that runs tests on every change, and we prepare publishing to pub.dev if you want it. The Basic, Standard and Premium packages differ in how many packages we deliver, how thorough the documentation is and whether platform code and publishing are included. When we extract a package from an existing app, we can also update that app to use it.

## Do and avoid

**Do:**
- Decide early whether the package is private or public.
- Keep the interface small and write examples before adding options.
- Use semantic versioning so that breaking changes are visible.
- Run the tests in your own pipeline after we hand it over.
- Choose a license deliberately if the package will be public.

**Avoid:**
- Putting app-specific code inside a shared package.
- Publishing a package with no tests or documentation.
- Depending on many third-party packages for small tasks.
- Changing the public interface without a version bump.
- Packaging code that is still changing every week.

## Who this service is for

An agency with several client apps that repeat the same screens. A company with a design system that wants consistent widgets across products. A developer who needs a plugin for a device feature, or who wants to publish a useful tool and have it built properly.

## What we need from you

A description of what the package should do, access to the apps or repositories that will use it as a collaborator, and your preferred naming and license. For extraction work, we need a read-write invitation to the source project. We never ask for passwords, and the code and package remain yours.
